gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 24?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent real-time observations from Munich-area stations and consensus from numerical weather models, including GFS runs, show surface temperatures peaking near 24 °C during the afternoon under mostly cloudy skies, moderate easterly flow, and dew points in the low teens °C. This aligns closely with the long-term August 24 climatological normal of 23.4 °C and explains the market’s near-certain pricing on that exact outcome. A modest diurnal range, limited insolation from cloud cover, and absence of strong warm advection have kept readings from exceeding or falling short of this threshold. Only an unexpected late-day clearing combined with stronger southerly winds or a localized station-specific anomaly could realistically shift the official daily maximum away from 24 °C before midnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources including GFS ensembles and European agencies project a daytime high near 22–23°C in Munich on August 25 under light winds, with possible early sprinkles and overcast conditions. These factors limit peak solar heating and favor slightly lower maxima around 19–20°C, aligning with the closely matched market-implied probabilities for those outcomes. Late-August climatology shows typical highs of 21–23°C, but reduced insolation from clouds can suppress temperatures by 1–3°C compared to clear-sky scenarios. Model spread and timing of any precipitation introduce genuine uncertainty, keeping trader consensus balanced between the leading bins while assigning lower odds to 21°C or warmer. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance ahead of resolution will refine the exact threshold.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the UK Met Office and other models points to a daytime maximum of 24–25°C in London on August 25, 2026, under largely settled conditions with sunny spells and light easterly or northeasterly winds.** 

Early morning readings near 16–17°C at stations such as Heathrow have been followed by steady daytime heating under mostly clear skies and low precipitation risk (<10–20% in afternoon hours). This aligns with above-average August conditions but well below recent heatwave peaks earlier in the month. 

Model runs show limited spread, with peak values hinging on exact cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing; slight differences in insolation or a brief increase in low-level moisture could tip the official high between 24°C and 25°C. The market-implied odds (24°C at 59%, 25°C at 31.5%) reflect this narrow uncertainty band and the “wisdom of crowds” assessment of real-time observational data releases, with lower probabilities assigned to cooler or warmer outliers given the stable high-pressure influence and absence of significant frontal activity. 

Upcoming Met Office updates and hourly station reports through the afternoon will provide the final resolution criteria.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models points to a maximum temperature of 33–35°C in Tokyo on August 26, supporting the near-even market split between those outcomes. Persistent summer high pressure and southerly flow have maintained recent daily highs near 33–35°C, yet increasing mid-level moisture and a 20–40% chance of scattered afternoon showers or cloud build-up could cap peak readings by 1–2°C. Model runs diverge on timing and coverage of convection, creating the close implied probabilities around the 34°C and 35°C thresholds while historical August averages near 31°C underscore the current elevated baseline. Updated JMA guidance and next model cycles will refine resolution criteria for the daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover and morning showers across Munich on August 25 are capping daytime heating, keeping the daily maximum near 19–21 °C and driving the near-even market split between 19 °C and 20 °C. Light westerly flow and high humidity further limit surface warming while scattered precipitation enhances evaporative cooling. Official guidance from the German Weather Service and GFS ensembles shows only modest afternoon clearing, with any breaks in the overcast offering the main pathway for a brief spike toward 21–22 °C. Traders are therefore weighting the likelihood of sustained stratus and rain-cooled air, which historically suppresses late-August maxima by 2–3 °C relative to clear-sky potential.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated high-resolution guidance tomorrow morning will further constrain resolution risk.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and the German Weather Service (DWD) have driven trader sentiment toward a daily maximum of 18–19 °C in Munich on August 25, 2026.** These outcomes currently command roughly two-thirds of the market probability, reflecting the latest model consensus on a cooler-than-climatological day.

Late-summer radiative cooling, combined with increased cloud cover and light northeasterly flow, has suppressed surface heating compared with earlier guidance that favored 21–23 °C. Ensemble spreads remain modest, with limited upside risk from clearing skies or stronger insolation, keeping the 20 °C and higher bins below 15 % combined. Historical late-August averages near 22–23 °C provide context, yet the current synoptic pattern—marked by a passing trough and modest moisture—has shifted probabilities downward over the past 48 hours. Traders are now focused on the final DWD and ECMWF updates, plus real-time observations, to confirm whether the high settles in the 18–19 °C range or edges slightly higher under any late-day clearing.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models indicate a shift toward increased cloud cover and scattered showers or thunderstorms over Tokyo on August 27, driven by a passing frontal system and moist southerly flow. This reduces incoming solar radiation and limits peak daytime heating compared to the clearer, hotter conditions of the prior days, with guidance converging on highs near 30–33 °C. High humidity and potential for early afternoon precipitation further suppress maximum temperatures, while minor model spread on exact timing and coverage of showers creates the observed tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 30–32 °C. Updated runs from official agencies and global models will refine these details ahead of resolution.

Final adjustments remain possible from overnight radiative cooling or convective timing, but consensus supports limited upside beyond 28°C.

**Forecast models and official guidance from the Met Office position London for a sunny day with a maximum temperature of 25–26°C.** Easterly winds and high pressure are delivering clear skies and limited cloud cover, supporting daytime warming to the mid-20s Celsius while keeping overnight lows near 17–18°C. This setup aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes at 24°C (53%) and 25°C (43%), as traders price in the consensus range from multiple model runs.

Late-August climatology for London typically peaks in the low-20s, but 2026’s preceding heatwave period has left a modestly elevated baseline that supports the slight upward bias in current guidance. Key resolution factors include the official daily maximum recorded at representative stations such as Heathrow or Kew; any late-day cloud build-up or stronger breeze could cap readings at 24°C, while full sunshine through peak heating hours favors 25°C. Updated Met Office and ECMWF runs released overnight have reinforced this narrow band, tightening implied probabilities around these two values ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Met Office and ensemble forecasts position London's August 26 maximum near 26°C, with sunny intervals giving way to increasing cloud and scattered showers as low pressure approaches from the south. Easterly to southeasterly flow is advecting milder air while added humidity and cloud cover cap peaks below recent warm spells, keeping most guidance between 25–27°C. Model agreement on these values, combined with historical August norms around 22–24°C, explains the market concentration on 25–27°C outcomes. Traders are weighting the latest 12Z runs and expected afternoon clearing against the small risk of heavier rain suppressing the high by 1–2°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Met Office, ECMWF, and GFS show London daytime highs on 27 August clustered around 24–26°C under a southwesterly flow and increasing cloud cover ahead of thundery showers. Consensus points to a warm but humid airmass with limited daytime heating once low cloud and scattered rain arrive, keeping peaks near seasonal norms rather than the warmer 26–27°C seen on preceding days. Key variables separating 24°C from 25°C outcomes include the exact timing and coverage of showers, which can suppress maxima by 1–2°C through reduced insolation, plus minor differences in how models handle boundary-layer moisture and wind shifts. Ensemble spreads remain modest but widen on cloud breaks that could allow brief warmer spells. Next operational runs and official Met Office guidance will further constrain resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models indicate London will likely see a daytime maximum of 24–26°C on August 27, 2026, with market-implied odds clustering tightly around 24°C (29%) and 25°C (30%).** This reflects genuine near-term uncertainty in how quickly thundery showers and increased cloud cover will arrive and suppress peak heating.

A transition from relatively settled high pressure earlier in the week to a more unsettled pattern is the dominant driver. Easterly to southeasterly winds are giving way to southerly and southwesterly flow, advecting warmer but moister air from the continent while increasing the likelihood of convective showers and thunderstorms, especially during the afternoon. Official guidance from the Met Office highlights a yellow thunderstorm warning and notes that daytime temperatures will remain near or slightly above seasonal normals (late-August London averages hover near 22–24°C), but heavy cloud and rainfall will limit surface heating.

Key variables differentiating the narrow range of outcomes include the precise timing, coverage, and intensity of showers: prolonged or widespread rain and thick stratiform cloud would favor the lower end (23–24°C) by reducing incoming solar radiation, while any breaks allowing stronger insolation could push readings to 25–26°C. Wind speed and direction also matter—lighter winds under broken cloud permit localized warming, whereas stronger southwesterlies enhance mixing and cooling. Ensemble spread in short-range models remains modest but sufficient to keep the two leading bins nearly even in trader consensus.

Upcoming high-resolution model runs and updated Met Office or ECMWF guidance over the next 24–48 hours will likely tighten the range as the exact evolution of the frontal system and associated convection becomes clearer. Historical analogs for late-August thundery breakdowns in southeast England show similar day-to-day variability in maxima of 2–3°C depending on convective timing.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models indicate London will likely see a daytime maximum of 24–26°C on August 27, 2026, with market-implied odds clustering tightly around 24°C (29%) and 25°C (30%).** This reflects genuine near-term uncertainty in how quickly thundery showers and increased cloud cover will arrive and suppress peak heating.

A transition from relatively settled high pressure earlier in the week to a more unsettled pattern is the dominant driver. Easterly to southeasterly winds are giving way to southerly and southwesterly flow, advecting warmer but moister air from the continent while increasing the likelihood of convective showers and thunderstorms, especially during the afternoon. Official guidance from the Met Office highlights a yellow thunderstorm warning and notes that daytime temperatures will remain near or slightly above seasonal normals (late-August London averages hover near 22–24°C), but heavy cloud and rainfall will limit surface heating.

Key variables differentiating the narrow range of outcomes include the precise timing, coverage, and intensity of showers: prolonged or widespread rain and thick stratiform cloud would favor the lower end (23–24°C) by reducing incoming solar radiation, while any breaks allowing stronger insolation could push readings to 25–26°C. Wind speed and direction also matter—lighter winds under broken cloud permit localized warming, whereas stronger southwesterlies enhance mixing and cooling. Ensemble spread in short-range models remains modest but sufficient to keep the two leading bins nearly even in trader consensus.

Upcoming high-resolution model runs and updated Met Office or ECMWF guidance over the next 24–48 hours will likely tighten the range as the exact evolution of the frontal system and associated convection becomes clearer. Historical analogs for late-August thundery breakdowns in southeast England show similar day-to-day variability in maxima of 2–3°C depending on convective timing.

Historical normals for late August (roughly 82°F average high) further anchor expectations, while today’s observed 81°F high under clear conditions supports continuity into tomorrow. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the Met Office and supporting models points to a daytime maximum of 26°C for London on August 26, 2026, with traders assigning the highest implied probability (42.5%) to that exact outcome.** 

Multiple runs show highs clustered between 25–27°C (combined ~88% probability), reflecting limited daytime heating from increasing cloud cover, scattered thundery showers, and easterly flow. The Met Office explicitly forecasts 26°C maximum under a yellow thunderstorm warning, with afternoon temperatures reaching the mid-20s before any showers develop. Supporting guidance from other sources aligns closely, citing mostly cloudy conditions, light rain or thunderstorms (50–70% chance), and southeast winds that keep marine influence modest while humidity rises. 

These conditions prevent stronger insolation that could push readings to 28°C or higher, while overnight lows near 18°C and the overall pattern keep sub-25°C outcomes less likely. Historical late-August averages sit around 21–22°C, so the current setup represents a modestly above-normal but capped warm spell ahead of a more unsettled period. Updated model runs and any shifts in shower timing remain the key variables that could nudge the final observed maximum within this narrow range.

**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's August 26 high temperature centers on official forecasts and short-range model consensus showing a likely peak of 34–35°C, with modest downside risk from afternoon cloud build-up.**

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) forecast issued August 25 projects a 35°C maximum under initially clear skies turning cloudy later, with precipitation probabilities rising from near 0% in the morning to 20–30% by afternoon. Private models and ensembles cluster in a similar range (roughly 33–36°C), reflecting a warm, humid southerly flow that supports high temperatures but allows scattered convection to develop and reduce peak insolation. Recent observed highs on August 25 reached 33–35°C under comparable conditions, providing a baseline for persistence.

The tight market spread—34°C at 36.5% implied probability edging 35°C at 28.5%—captures residual uncertainty in exact timing of cloud cover, storm initiation, and the influence of Tokyo’s urban heat island on the official measurement site. Higher outcomes (36°C+) carry lower odds because sustained clear skies and stronger insolation would be required, while lower results remain possible if showers arrive earlier than modeled. Traders are effectively pricing the JMA call plus ensemble spread rather than any single outlier run. New JMA updates and afternoon model runs on August 26 will be the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent summer heat moderated by incoming moisture and instability is the main driver keeping trader focus tightly clustered around 30–32°C for Tokyo’s August 27 maximum.** Recent model runs from the Japan Meteorological Agency and international ensembles show a transition from hot, mostly clear conditions on the 25–26th (forecast highs 33–34°C) to increasing cloud cover, humidity, and a 65–85% probability of afternoon showers or thunderstorms on the 27th. These factors limit surface heating through reduced insolation and evaporative cooling, capping the daily peak near or slightly below the seasonal average of ~31°C. Minor differences among 30°C, 31°C, and 32°C outcomes hinge on the precise timing and intensity of convective activity, which can suppress the high by 1–3°C if storms develop earlier or intensify. Current ensemble spread and short-range updates from the National Hurricane Center’s Pacific analogs plus JMA guidance keep the market-implied odds closely matched while highlighting the sensitivity of the daily maximum to precipitation onset.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent summer heat moderated by incoming moisture and instability is the main driver keeping trader focus tightly clustered around 30–32°C for Tokyo’s August 27 maximum.** Recent model runs from the Japan Meteorological Agency and international ensembles show a transition from hot, mostly clear conditions on the 25–26th (forecast highs 33–34°C) to increasing cloud cover, humidity, and a 65–85% probability of afternoon showers or thunderstorms on the 27th. These factors limit surface heating through reduced insolation and evaporative cooling, capping the daily peak near or slightly below the seasonal average of ~31°C. Minor differences among 30°C, 31°C, and 32°C outcomes hinge on the precise timing and intensity of convective activity, which can suppress the high by 1–3°C if storms develop earlier or intensify. Current ensemble spread and short-range updates from the National Hurricane Center’s Pacific analogs plus JMA guidance keep the market-implied odds closely matched while highlighting the sensitivity of the daily maximum to precipitation onset.
